references.text: Isaiah prophesies about the Redeemer who will come to Zion: [ref:Jes 59:20|Isaiah 59:20]. The Emmaus disciples had hoped that Jesus was the one who would "redeem" (λυτροῦσθαι) Israel, reflecting the expectation of the promised Redeemer.

Israel's expectation that God would redeem Jerusalem: [ref:Jes 52:9|Isaiah 52:9]. The Emmaus disciples' hope that Jesus would deliver Israel is connected to this Old Testament expectation of redemption.
God promised to redeem Israel from slavery in Egypt: [ref:2 Mos 6:6|Exodus 6:6]. The word "redeem" (λυτροῦσθαι) in Luke 24:21 builds on this fundamental concept of God's redemption of His people.
The psalmist expresses the hope that the Lord will redeem Israel from all its sins: [ref:Sal 130:7-8|Psalm 130:7-8]. The Emmaus disciples shared this hope for Israel's redemption.

Zechariah's song of praise at John's birth proclaims that God has visited and redeemed His people: [ref:Luk 1:68|Luke 1:68]. The expectation of redemption expressed at Jesus' birth is the same as what the Emmaus disciples voiced.
The prophetess Anna spoke about the child Jesus to all who were waiting for Jerusalem's redemption: [ref:Luk 2:38|Luke 2:38]. The Emmaus disciples' hope reflects this same messianic expectation.

Jesus Himself explains that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day: [ref:Luk 24:46|Luke 24:46]. The reference to the "third day" in verse 21 points forward to Jesus' own explanation of the resurrection.

Even after the resurrection, the disciples ask if Jesus will now restore the kingdom for Israel: [ref:Apg 1:6|Acts 1:6]. This shows that the expectation of Israel's redemption, expressed in Luke 24:21, continued to shape the disciples' thinking.

Hosea prophesies that the Lord will make alive after two days and raise up on the third day: [ref:Hos 6:2|Hosea 6:2]. The Emmaus disciples' remark that it is now the "third day" can be seen in light of this prophecy of restoration.

Jesus predicted His suffering, death, and resurrection on the third day: [ref:Matt 16:21|Matthew 16:21]. The Emmaus disciples' reference to the third day corresponds with Jesus' own predictions about His resurrection.
Jesus predicts again that He will be handed over, crucified, and rise on the third day: [ref:Matt 20:19|Matthew 20:19]. The time indication "third day" in Luke 24:21 aligns with these predictions.

Paul confesses that Christ was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures: [ref:1 Kor 15:4|1 Corinthians 15:4]. The third day mentioned by the Emmaus disciples is precisely the day when the resurrection took place, according to the apostolic confession.
